31 In the circuit shown, lamp P is rated 250 V, 50 W and lamp Q is rated 250 V, 200 W. The two
lamps are connected in series to a 250 V power supply.
250 V
P
Q
Assume that the resistance of each lamp remains constant.
Which statement most accurately describes what happens when the switch is closed?
A
Lamp P emits four times as much power as lamp Q.
B
Lamp P emits twice as much power as lamp Q.
C
Lamp Q emits four times as much power as lamp P.
D
Lamp Q emits twice as much power as lamp P.

hints: Compare the $250\text{ V}$, $50\text{ W}$ rating of P with the $250\text{ V}$, $200\text{ W}$ rating of Q using $P = V^2/R$ to see which filament has the larger resistance.
Remember P and Q are in series to the $250\text{ V}$ supply, so the current $I$ through them is identical and $P = I^2R$ controls the actual power.
Form the resistance ratio $R_P/R_Q$ from $R = V^2/P$ and use it as the actual power ratio $P_P/P_Q$ for the same current.
walkthrough: Find each filament resistance from its rating using $P = V^2/R$, rearranged to $R = V^2/P$ with $V = 250\text{ V}$.
When the switch is closed P and Q are in series, so the same current $I$ flows through both.
Actual dissipated power is $P = I^2R$, so $P_P/P_Q = I^2R_P/I^2R_Q = R_P/R_Q = 4$.
Thus lamp P, the $50\text{ W}$ rated lamp with higher resistance, emits four times as much power as lamp Q. This is option A.

A.explanation: In series the current $I$ is the same, and with $P = I^2R$ the lamp with four times the resistance dissipates four times the power, which is lamp P.

B.explanation: The power ratio in series equals the resistance ratio, which is $200/50 = 4$, not 2.

C.explanation: Lamp Q has the larger rated power at $250\text{ V}$ so it has the smaller resistance and dissipates less power for the same series current.

D.explanation: Lamp Q cannot emit more power in series because its resistance is smaller, and the factor is 4 not 2.
